item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
Consensus is slow by design.

In crypto, we’ve accepted the tradeoff: robustness at the cost of speed. Whether it’s proof-of-work or proof-of-stake, every node reprocesses every transaction, every time. It’s secure and reliable... but often overkill for most of what we actually do.

What if we stopped treating every transaction like a global event? What if the base layer didn’t have to decide who bought a coffee first, especially when those transactions have nothing to do with each other?

Pod Network offers an alternative closer to a network of local agreements, where state can move fast, stay composable, and only invoke ordering when absolutely necessary.

We sat down with Shresth Agarwal at ETHDenver to talk about rethinking onchain design. If you’ve ever thought about the limits of blockspace, MEV, or how far we can push latency while keeping decentralization intact, this conversation is going to give you something new to think about.

item.title: Uniswap, Ekubo, and the Rise Of Innovative DEX Designs
item.description:
What if DEXs could do more?

Ekubo thinks they can. Their approach? Dedefining efficiency from the ground up, from memory architecture to fee mechanics, decreasing gas costs while unlocking features like TWAMs.

In today’s episode, we sit down with Moody, Ekubo's founder and Uniswap v3 co-author, alongside Benjamin Sturisky from the Starknet Foundation.

We explore why they chose Starknet over Ethereum mainnet, reflecting shared values around validity rollups, Cairo optimization, and account abstraction.

Our conversation covers capital-efficient liquidity, revenue models, the appchain vs. shared ecosystem debate, token launches, and the practical economics of building protocols that work in the real world.

Let's jump in.

item.title: Can Solana Replace NASDAQ? With Max Resnick and Logan Jastremski
item.description:
What kind of infrastructure do we actually need to support real, global trading onchain?

In today's episode, we dig into the debate between high-throughput blockchains and modular approaches with Logan and Max, both vocal Solana supporters. They share why they believe monolithic scaling is the way to go, and why Solana is aiming to replace NASDAQ, not Ethereum. (Yes!)

We discuss how global data synchronization at the speed of light could lead to fairer markets with tighter spreads, potentially beating traditional exchanges. We also cover MEV extraction on Solana, its evolving social layer following the Trump coin surge, and why the recent inflation reduction proposal didn't succeed.

Let's dive in.

item.itunes:summary:
What kind of infrastructure do we actually need to support real, global trading onchain?

In today's episode, we dig into the debate between high-throughput blockchains and modular approaches with Logan and Max, both vocal Solana supporters. They share why they believe monolithic scaling is the way to go, and why Solana is aiming to replace NASDAQ, not Ethereum. (Yes!)

We discuss how global data synchronization at the speed of light could lead to fairer markets with tighter spreads, potentially beating traditional exchanges. We also cover MEV extraction on Solana, its evolving social layer following the Trump coin surge, and why the recent inflation reduction proposal didn't succeed.

Let's dive in.

item.title: Ram Kumar on AGI, Specialized Intelligence, and Agent Infrastructure
item.description:
Now that the Crypto AI peak of inflated expectations has passed, what’s actually built to last?

In today's episode, we are looking at the real infrastructure needed for long-term AI projects.

We sit down with Ram Kumar of OpenLedger to explore how their team is building AI that actually understands crypto, not just slapping ChatGPT onto existing apps. OpenLedger is designing intelligence that’s native to DeFi and blockchain, not retrofitted for it.

This shift from generic AI to systems that truly grasp DeFi mechanics and blockchain architecture isn’t just a nice-to-have. It’s a necessity. And it opens the door for something bigger: specialized AI agents that collaborate with each other in real time.

Let's jump in.

item.title: Are Stablecoins & RWAs Crypto’s Main Use Case? with Chris Yin
item.description:
Crypto has always been a game of extremes. On one end, a memecoins casino and speculative madness; on the other, an attempt to build something more sustainable.

In today's episode, we sit down with Chris Yin, co-founder and CEO of Plume Network, to cut through the noise around RWAs. Chris explains why most RWA projects are just "TradFi people doing TradFi stuff on chain" and why that approach is missing the point entirely.

From the reality behind BlackRock's crypto plays to why stable coins remain the only RWA that truly matters, Chris shares an insider's perspective on building infrastructure that brings real-world value on chain - the right way.

We also dive into the challenges of building sustainable crypto products, why bottom-up adoption beats institutional onboarding, and what assets beyond T-bills actually make sense to tokenize.

Let's get into it.

item.itunes:summary:
Crypto has always been a game of extremes. On one end, a memecoins casino and speculative madness; on the other, an attempt to build something more sustainable.

In today's episode, we sit down with Chris Yin, co-founder and CEO of Plume Network, to cut through the noise around RWAs. Chris explains why most RWA projects are just "TradFi people doing TradFi stuff on chain" and why that approach is missing the point entirely.

From the reality behind BlackRock's crypto plays to why stable coins remain the only RWA that truly matters, Chris shares an insider's perspective on building infrastructure that brings real-world value on chain - the right way.

We also dive into the challenges of building sustainable crypto products, why bottom-up adoption beats institutional onboarding, and what assets beyond T-bills actually make sense to tokenize.

Let's get into it.

item.title: Is Crypto's Biggest Payment Problem Already Solved? With Paul Faecks
item.description:
While everyone's attention has been focused the current market volatility, stablecoins have been thriving.

In today's episode, we take a look at Plasma and uncover what their team has been working on for stablecoins. Rather than creating another all-purpose blockchain, they've developed something specifically for stablecoin payments. Zero fee USDT transfers in a system built for speed, affordability, and high volume.

We spoke with Paul, founder of Plasma, about USDT's growing dominance in global payments, the daily transfer limitations of networks like Ethereum and Tron, and Plasma's overall approach. Paul also shares valuable insights on institutional adoption of stablecoins as well as how Bitcoin could become involved.

The next step for stablecoins is just around the corner.

Let's dive in.

item.title: Why A 'Return To Fundamentals' in Crypto Is Imminent with YQ
item.description:
What makes crypto so different in the East and the West?

In the U.S. and Europe, teams typically focus on building the foundation: rollups, restaking, scaling solutions. In Asia, markets drive adoption, trading volume, and unique market trends.

We sat with YQ, founder of AltLayer, to dive deeper. Western builders think ahead, prioritizing scalability and decentralization. Eastern markets excel at liquidity, with efficient capital flow and rapidly emerging trends.

This global dynamic shapes both development and investment strategies. Understanding it is essential for anyone interested in crypto.

item.itunes:summary:
What makes crypto so different in the East and the West?

In the U.S. and Europe, teams typically focus on building the foundation: rollups, restaking, scaling solutions. In Asia, markets drive adoption, trading volume, and unique market trends.

We sat with YQ, founder of AltLayer, to dive deeper. Western builders think ahead, prioritizing scalability and decentralization. Eastern markets excel at liquidity, with efficient capital flow and rapidly emerging trends.

This global dynamic shapes both development and investment strategies. Understanding it is essential for anyone interested in crypto.

item.title: Berachain's DeFi Summer 2.0 Playbook with Smokey the Bera
item.description:
What if DeFi value flowed back to its users?

In today’s episode, we’re exploring the Berachain ecosystem with its founder, Smokey The Bera, to dive into this idea and talk about the chain’s rapid growth.

Berachain is different. It’s built on a unique symbiotic relationship between the chain, validators, and apps. By using game theory, it lets users create strategies based on the tokens they want to optimize and their risk preferences.

We also dig into how Berachain's flow mechanism works, where apps revenue flows straight back to BGT holders, and touch on things like pre-deposit vaults, the formation of ecosystem alliances, unexpected institutional interest, and how PayPal USD is finding a new home on Berachain.

Let's dive in.

item.title: Why An Explosion of User-Owned AI Is Coming with Illia Polosukhin
item.description:
An AI agent with no hidden motives or data harvesting. Dream or reality?

In today's episode, we talk with Illia Polosukhin, co-founder of NEAR Protocol, about the idea of having your own AI.

That's exactly what NEAR has created with their AI Transaction Protocol (AITP). They have an open ecosystem where AI systems can communicate and transact while you maintain complete control.

NEAR isn't just developing better AI technology, they're also ensuring that automated systems remain open, verifiable, and in your hands rather than locked behind corporate walls.

Join us on how NEAR's blockchain foundation enables user-owned AI and why this matters moving forward.

An AI agent with no hidden motives or data harvesting. Dream or reality?

In today's episode, we talk with Illia Polosukhin, co-founder of NEAR Protocol, about the idea of having your own AI.

That's exactly what NEAR has created with their AI Transaction Protocol (AITP). They have an open ecosystem where AI systems can communicate and transact while you maintain complete control.

NEAR isn't just developing better AI technology, they're also ensuring that automated systems remain open, verifiable, and in your hands rather than locked behind corporate walls.

Join us on how NEAR's blockchain foundation enables user-owned AI and why this matters moving forward.

item.title: Alex Gluchowski and Sreeram Kannan on Their Collaborative Scaling Vision
item.description:
ZK needs decentralized proving networks, or we're just moving trust to a new bottleneck.

Same goes for L2s.

In today's episode, we cover how EigenLayer attempts to create a new way to coordinate decentralized proving networks so no single entity controls the backbone of ZK systems.

We sit down with zkSync co-inventor, Alex Gluchowski and EigenLayer founder, Sreeram to cover how modular scaling works, why decentralizing proof generation matters, what this means for DeFi builders wanting flexibility without sacrificing security, and more.

This conversation drills into modular design and the future of verifiable computation.

item.title: How Initia’s Interwoven Economy Is Defying Traditional Multi-Chain Design with Zon
item.description:
In today's episode, we sit down with Intia co-founder, Zon, to talk about what Initia is cooking.

The Initia team has been busy building their interwoven rollup ecosystem with 15 publicly announced rollups and a massive $26 million invested. Rollups on Initia have raised more than even Initia itself, showing clear interest.

We look into Initia's VIP Program, why high staking rates are hurting DeFi ecosystems, how Initia plans to boost economic velocity, and why they believe purpose-built chains will win over the "we're faster than everyone else" crowd.

Are we finally seeing a shift from speculation-driven approaches to systems that reward actual usage?

Let's explore.

item.itunes:summary:
In today's episode, we sit down with Intia co-founder, Zon, to talk about what Initia is cooking.

The Initia team has been busy building their interwoven rollup ecosystem with 15 publicly announced rollups and a massive $26 million invested. Rollups on Initia have raised more than even Initia itself, showing clear interest.

We look into Initia's VIP Program, why high staking rates are hurting DeFi ecosystems, how Initia plans to boost economic velocity, and why they believe purpose-built chains will win over the "we're faster than everyone else" crowd.

Are we finally seeing a shift from speculation-driven approaches to systems that reward actual usage?

Let's explore.

item.title: Terence Kwok on Digital Identity, Proof of Personhood, and Eastern Crypto Markets
item.description:
The line between real humans and bots is blurring.

In today’s episode, we chat with Terence Kwok, the founder of Humanity Protocol, to explore how they're balancing privacy and accountability. Humanity is using technology to read palm prints and vein patterns for verification, all without storing biometric data.

This approach could offer a way for users to prove they’re not bots without compromising their personal information. We look into Humanity Protocol's approach, technology, and place in the evolving landscape.

Let's get into it.

item.title: Rich Rines on Bitcoin's Path to $1,000,000
item.description:
In today's episode, we talk about the Bitcoin dilemma.

Despite it being crypto's foundation, it mainly sits unused in cold storage wasting away any potential. Between high fees, slow transactions, and lack of use case, Bitcoin has struggled to evolve past being a store of value.

We sit down with Rich Rines of Core DAO to learn how they are unlocking Bitcoin's potential towards delivering structured products, derivatives, and staking.

We also cover how Core connects Bitcoin to onchain finance, their liquid staking token (lstBTC), institutional partnerships, and much more.

Let's jump in.

item.itunes:summary:
In today's episode, we talk about the Bitcoin dilemma.

Despite it being crypto's foundation, it mainly sits unused in cold storage wasting away any potential. Between high fees, slow transactions, and lack of use case, Bitcoin has struggled to evolve past being a store of value.

We sit down with Rich Rines of Core DAO to learn how they are unlocking Bitcoin's potential towards delivering structured products, derivatives, and staking.

We also cover how Core connects Bitcoin to onchain finance, their liquid staking token (lstBTC), institutional partnerships, and much more.

Let's jump in.

item.title: How Kaito Built an InfoFi Economy with Yu Hu
item.description:
In today's episode, we cover what happens when you tokenize attention.

We sat down with Yu Hu to get the inside story of how Kaito went from tracking crypto Twitter sentiment to dropping what might be the most widely distributed token in recent history. It's completely reshaping how value flows through the crypto social layer.

Kaito leans into using market forces and onchain mechanics to cut through the noise and find signal. And they're just getting started too. They have plans to move beyond Crypto Twitter into TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube as well.

While other similar project crash and burn, Kaito is positioned for longevity because there's real value being generated underneath all the hype.

Let's dive in.

item.title: Amanda Cassatt on Crypto’s Branding Problem, Scaling Serotonin, and Yapping
item.description:
In today's episode, we feature a conversation with the strategist behind Ethereum's early marketing initiatives—Amanda Cassatt. She covers her career progression towards becoming the influential figure who helped establish Ethereum as a recognized name in technology, rather than just a hacker project (as it was in its early days).

Amanda takes us through her professional background from serving as ConsenSys CMO to establishing Serotonin, offering valuable perspectives on the distinguishing factors between successful and unsuccessful web3 ventures.

We also discuss current landscape surrounding token launches, strategies to reach new audiences, how to think about launching brands in crypto, the problem of communication without substance in the industry, and Amanda's insights into the future technological stratification expressed as positioning "above or below the API line."

This one got spicy, and trippy. It was fun.

This discussion reveals the core components required to develop a successful crypto brand during a time where the space is littered with projects that offer surface-level activity without meaningful value or strong foundation.

We don’t love being cynical, but sometimes you need to call a spade, a spade.

We did that today. Enjoy.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
In today's episode, we feature a conversation with the strategist behind Ethereum's early marketing initiatives—Amanda Cassatt. She covers her career progression towards becoming the influential figure who helped establish Ethereum as a recognized name in technology, rather than just a hacker project (as it was in its early days).

Amanda takes us through her professional background from serving as ConsenSys CMO to establishing Serotonin, offering valuable perspectives on the distinguishing factors between successful and unsuccessful web3 ventures.

We also discuss current landscape surrounding token launches, strategies to reach new audiences, how to think about launching brands in crypto, the problem of communication without substance in the industry, and Amanda's insights into the future technological stratification expressed as positioning "above or below the API line."

This one got spicy, and trippy. It was fun.

This discussion reveals the core components required to develop a successful crypto brand during a time where the space is littered with projects that offer surface-level activity without meaningful value or strong foundation.

We don’t love being cynical, but sometimes you need to call a spade, a spade.

We did that today. Enjoy.

item.title: Yat Siu on East vs. West Culture, Neo-Capitalism, and Onchain Property Rights
item.description:
Hong Kong is strategically positioning itself as a key web3 hub, and there are good reasons to watch what's happening there.

A major highlight from Consensus Hong Kong is the quickly evolving regulatory landscape. Recently, Animoca Brands teamed up with Standard Chartered and Hong Kong Telecom to launch a regulated HKD stablecoin – one of the first with direct backing from a major bank and official HKMA regulation.

The bigger picture? Network effects drive success. Whether it's stablecoins bringing new users onboard or Web3 gaming driving engagement, long-term winners are those building lasting communities and sustainable economies.

That's what we're diving into today with Animoca Brands Chairman, Yat Siu. We get deep into Hong Kong's emergence as a web3 center, shifting views on stablecoins, and how crypto adoption in Asia differs from Western markets.

Let's jump in.

item.title: How To Find A Massive Edge in Crypto with Akshat Vaidya
item.description:
In today’s episode, we take a dive through the founders journey and what it’s like to run a massive crypto fund.

Clearly, crypto cycles follow a pattern.

Skepticism transforms into celebration, then a cooldown period, until something innovative emerges to change the landscape. Each of these cycle presents distinct opportunities.

That is what we discuss in today's episode with Akshat Vaidya from Maelstorm. We cover navigating from early Bitcoin through the DeFi expansion into staking infrastructure and how one's approach tends to evolve with each market phase. Akshat has spent years in onchain investing—identifying overlooked value, recognizing cycle timing, and determining which innovations demonstrate staying power.

We look at potential future directions for crypto. Liquid staking, onchain real-world assets, the increasing convergence between traditional venture capital and crypto markets.

We touch on crypto M&A, selling businesses and psychedelics as well.

Let's explore.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
In today’s episode, we take a dive through the founders journey and what it’s like to run a massive crypto fund.

Clearly, crypto cycles follow a pattern.

Skepticism transforms into celebration, then a cooldown period, until something innovative emerges to change the landscape. Each of these cycle presents distinct opportunities.

That is what we discuss in today's episode with Akshat Vaidya from Maelstorm. We cover navigating from early Bitcoin through the DeFi expansion into staking infrastructure and how one's approach tends to evolve with each market phase. Akshat has spent years in onchain investing—identifying overlooked value, recognizing cycle timing, and determining which innovations demonstrate staying power.

We look at potential future directions for crypto. Liquid staking, onchain real-world assets, the increasing convergence between traditional venture capital and crypto markets.

We touch on crypto M&A, selling businesses and psychedelics as well.

Let's explore.

item.title: Kain Warwick on The Crime Cycle, Memes vs. Fundamentals, and SOL vs. ETH Culture
item.description:
For today’s episode, we look to answer the question “Seriously. What happened to crypto?” alongside Kain.

The landscape continues to evolve rapidly as underlying dynamics shift, narratives transform, capital redirects, and new market structures emerge.

In today's episode, we sit down with Kain Warwick from Infinex to cover the state of the market and look at how low-float VC okens have declined, memes have gained massive popularity, and Solana has become a primary venue for speculative trading and, well crime.

We uncover how the Ethereum and Solana social layers adapt to these changes, analyze persistent speculative activity, and identify what cyclical patterns indicate about market development looking ahead.

This is one you won’t want to miss.

item.title: Is Hibachi The Next Hyperliquid?
item.description:
Imagine Hyperliquid, but ZK.

In today's episode, we cover the evolution of onchain trading and its core challenge: balancing speed with security. It's a constant trade-off in DeFi. Faster systems, like Hyperliquid, tend to lean towards centralization, while more secure ones often sacrifice performance.

But there's a solution emerging: Boundless execution with ZK proofs.

This gives traders CEX-level execution while keeping funds verifiable. This approach also scales limitlessly with new nodes added to the system.

Join us as we chat with Hashflow CEO: Varun Kumar, Hibachi Co-Founder: Thibault Binier, and Boundless Product Lead: Jacob Everly to break down innovations in zk Apps.

If you're serious about the future of onchain trading, this one's for you.

item.itunes:summary:
Imagine Hyperliquid, but ZK.

In today's episode, we cover the evolution of onchain trading and its core challenge: balancing speed with security. It's a constant trade-off in DeFi. Faster systems, like Hyperliquid, tend to lean towards centralization, while more secure ones often sacrifice performance.

But there's a solution emerging: Boundless execution with ZK proofs.

This gives traders CEX-level execution while keeping funds verifiable. This approach also scales limitlessly with new nodes added to the system.

Join us as we chat with Hashflow CEO: Varun Kumar, Hibachi Co-Founder: Thibault Binier, and Boundless Product Lead: Jacob Everly to break down innovations in zk Apps.

If you're serious about the future of onchain trading, this one's for you.

item.title: Why BlackRock’s BUIDL Fund is Going Multichain
item.description:
In today's episode, we cover how regulation meets the greater crypto economy.

Treasury tokens have evolved from concept to reality, now trading actively in DeFi markets with BlackRock and Securitize leading the transformation. By converting U.S. treasuries into blockchain assets with institutional backing, they're laying groundwork for wider adoption.

We sat down with Robinson Burkey, Co-Founder & CCO of Wormhole and Carlos Domingo, CEO of Securitize to go over how utility drives this innovation through cross-chain accessibility and DeFi integration, establishing these tokens as foundational collateral infrastructure. Robinson highlights seamless cross-chain movement as being critical, while Carlos points out institutions shift from viewing blockchain as merely an efficiency tool to seeing it as an opportunity engine.

Though regulatory, KYC, and institutional barriers persist, the momentum continues building.

Let's explore further.

item.title: The Seismic Shift in Infra Investing with Wyatt Lonergan & Xiang Xie
item.description:
In today’s episode, we explore the future of building infra for compliance, and the next era of investing following the massive infra wave of 2017-2024.


Typically, in crypto there have always been tradeoffs…


Want transparency? You lose privacy. Want privacy? Regulators get nervous.


Join us as we chat with Wyatt from VanEck Ventures and Xiang Xie from Primus dive into how Primus is using ZKTLS and ZKFHE to transform blockchain data integrity.


While traditional systems expose sensitive data through oracles, ZKTLS proves authenticity without revealing the underlying info. Add in ZKFHE's encrypted data computation, and we're looking at a game-changer for onchain finance (according to institutional investors).


We break down the investment thesis in Primus and cover insights on crypto infrastructure funding as a whole. We also explore how privacy-preserving financial infrastructure fits into the regulatory landscape, from payment systems to stablecoins and KYC.


Plus, we'll tackle the exciting fusion of ZK tech and AI in crypto, showing how it's revolutionizing everything from AI verification to streamlined, privacy-focused KYC.


Enjoy.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
In today’s episode, we explore the future of building infra for compliance, and the next era of investing following the massive infra wave of 2017-2024.


Typically, in crypto there have always been tradeoffs…


Want transparency? You lose privacy. Want privacy? Regulators get nervous.


Join us as we chat with Wyatt from VanEck Ventures and Xiang Xie from Primus dive into how Primus is using ZKTLS and ZKFHE to transform blockchain data integrity.


While traditional systems expose sensitive data through oracles, ZKTLS proves authenticity without revealing the underlying info. Add in ZKFHE's encrypted data computation, and we're looking at a game-changer for onchain finance (according to institutional investors).


We break down the investment thesis in Primus and cover insights on crypto infrastructure funding as a whole. We also explore how privacy-preserving financial infrastructure fits into the regulatory landscape, from payment systems to stablecoins and KYC.


Plus, we'll tackle the exciting fusion of ZK tech and AI in crypto, showing how it's revolutionizing everything from AI verification to streamlined, privacy-focused KYC.


Enjoy.

item.title: Justin Drake & Federico Carrone on Ethereum’s Native Rollup Roadmap
item.description:
For today’s episode, we take a deep dive into native rollups.

While rollups improved Ethereum's scaling, they introduced key challenges like centralized control, MEV extraction, buggy execution, and fragmented liquidity across layers.

Luckily, there's a new method aiming to maintain rollup benefits while eliminating these issues.

Native rollups and based sequencing offer a solution. By integrating directly with Ethereum, native rollups simplify operations and enhance security. Based sequencing lets Ethereum validators manage transaction ordering, improving L2 coordination.

Teams are also considering shifting away from centralized sequencing for regulatory compliance.

We sat down to chat with Justin Drake from the Ethereum Foundation and Fede to discuss this rapid transition and its implications for Ethereum's future as well as key insights for anyone following Ethereum's scaling evolution.

Let's get into it.

item.title: How ZK Will Power Bitcoin’s Next Era of Scaling
item.description:
Bitcoin has dominated crypto, but has remained largely inactive in DeFi. While ETH and Solana lead in onchain activity, a significant amount of BTC remains unused.

BitVM introduces a solution. Unlike traditional custodians or multi-sig bridges, it provides a trust-minimized approach to integrating BTC with DeFi – expanding Bitcoin's utility beyond just a store of value.

We spoke with Alexei (Bob), Yovela (Fiamma), and Jacob (Boundless) to examine BitVM's mechanics, its place in Bitcoin's scaling roadmap, and its implications for users seeking secure yield opportunities.

For those following Bitcoin rollups and the technical barriers to BTC adoption in DeFi, this discussion offers valuable insights.

Let's begin.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
Bitcoin has dominated crypto, but has remained largely inactive in DeFi. While ETH and Solana lead in onchain activity, a significant amount of BTC remains unused.

BitVM introduces a solution. Unlike traditional custodians or multi-sig bridges, it provides a trust-minimized approach to integrating BTC with DeFi – expanding Bitcoin's utility beyond just a store of value.

We spoke with Alexei (Bob), Yovela (Fiamma), and Jacob (Boundless) to examine BitVM's mechanics, its place in Bitcoin's scaling roadmap, and its implications for users seeking secure yield opportunities.

For those following Bitcoin rollups and the technical barriers to BTC adoption in DeFi, this discussion offers valuable insights.

Let's begin.

item.title: How Shogun Is Using Intents To Power a New Crypto UX
item.description:
Moving between chains is a hassle.

Whether you're swapping, bridging, or managing liquidity across ecosystems, users face clunky interfaces, slow execution, and unnecessary risks. What if that friction disappeared?

Enter Shogun, a trading platform that makes every chain feel like one. Using intent-based execution, automated routing, and solver-driven auctions, Shogun lets traders move assets smoothly across Solana, Ethereum, Move-based chains, and new rollups. No more juggling wallets, bridge delays, or split liquidity.

The concept is straightforward: Specify what you want, and Shogun finds the best way there. It uses TEV (Trader Extractable Value) to optimize trades for user benefit rather than extract value. By combining centralized and decentralized solvers, trades settle faster and more efficiently.

This could be the next step toward a true single-chain experience. With integrations on Phantom, MetaMask, and Telegram, it meets traders where they are.

What happens when trading across chains becomes as simple as trading on one?

Let's get into it.

item.title: The Bittensor Bull Thesis with James Ross and Mog
item.description:
For today's episode, we dive deep into the the intersection of AI and crypto, and discuss how this sector has produced more hype than results (so far).

While both fields promise decentralization, combining them effectively has proven challenging. Most projects either centralize AI decision-making or create token systems without clear utility.

Bittensor is taking a different approach to this problem by creating a network where AI models compete for rewards through market incentives. This system lets token holders decide which models receive rewards based on measurable performance, rather than promises or marketing.

Their recent update shifted voting power from validators to token holders, aiming to align incentives more directly with utility. One project testing this approach is Mode, with their new subnet Synth, an AI model competing to predict market volatility.

The Synth subnet is live, with data scientists building rival prediction models. Models face off in open competition with market-driven feedback, creating natural selection—strong performers earn more rewards, while weaker ones get filtered out.

Let’s dive into what this means, how Synth is applying it, and what’s next for onchain AI.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
For today's episode, we dive deep into the the intersection of AI and crypto, and discuss how this sector has produced more hype than results (so far).

While both fields promise decentralization, combining them effectively has proven challenging. Most projects either centralize AI decision-making or create token systems without clear utility.

Bittensor is taking a different approach to this problem by creating a network where AI models compete for rewards through market incentives. This system lets token holders decide which models receive rewards based on measurable performance, rather than promises or marketing.

Their recent update shifted voting power from validators to token holders, aiming to align incentives more directly with utility. One project testing this approach is Mode, with their new subnet Synth, an AI model competing to predict market volatility.

The Synth subnet is live, with data scientists building rival prediction models. Models face off in open competition with market-driven feedback, creating natural selection—strong performers earn more rewards, while weaker ones get filtered out.

Let’s dive into what this means, how Synth is applying it, and what’s next for onchain AI.

item.title: Inside Frax's Vision for Institutional Stablecoins with Sam Kazemian
item.description:
The stablecoin landscape is evolving as DeFi and traditional finance continue to merge.

Today we chat with Sam Kazemian from Frax to break down what's happening in the space. We'll dive into their new FRX USD launch and explore an interesting idea: using stablecoins to bridge the gap between crypto and U.S. treasuries.

Sam also walks us through how Frax is rethinking stablecoin design to make yield more accessible, while partnering with big players like BlackRock and SuperState. Sam also shares insights on stablecoins' potential to reshape the broader financial system beyond just crypto.

If you’ve been thinking about where stablecoins are headed, this is one to tune into.

item.title: Purpose-Built AI Chains with Anish Agnihotri and Saneel Seerni of Ritual
item.description:
AI and crypto are finally converging beyond just trading bots. Purpose-built chains like Ritual are enabling AI-powered smart contracts that can adapt in real-time – think automated trading strategies that adjust to market conditions or DeFi positions that manage themselves.

In our chat with Ritual founders Anish and Saneel, they explained how they're making AI decisions verifiable onchain. Their approach: smart contracts that can upgrade themselves based on market conditions and user behavior, but with guardrails to keep things secure.

The future of DeFAI (DeFi + AI) is starting to take shape, but important questions remain around security and automated financial control. Here's where we are and where we're headed.

item.itunes:summary:
AI and crypto are finally converging beyond just trading bots. Purpose-built chains like Ritual are enabling AI-powered smart contracts that can adapt in real-time – think automated trading strategies that adjust to market conditions or DeFi positions that manage themselves.

In our chat with Ritual founders Anish and Saneel, they explained how they're making AI decisions verifiable onchain. Their approach: smart contracts that can upgrade themselves based on market conditions and user behavior, but with guardrails to keep things secure.

The future of DeFAI (DeFi + AI) is starting to take shape, but important questions remain around security and automated financial control. Here's where we are and where we're headed.

item.title: What Community-Owned AI Really Means with Ben Parr
item.description:
For today’s episode, we are digging up our latest knowledge of AI and DeSci.

Yesnoerror is flipping the script on research validation.

Instead of traditional AI fact-checkers, they're letting the research community influence what gets verified next.

Their AI agent, as co-founder Ben Parr explains, digs through millions of papers catching details human reviewers might overlook. Every check is transparent and incentivized through tokens, keeping everyone honest.

By leveraging blockchain, YNE bypasses longstanding academic headaches by providing fast and reliable research validation without holdups. This goes beyond catching errorss. This is about accelerating science through open verification.

As autonomous agents grow more common, YNE's trust-building approach could shape how we handle AI systems across the board.

Let's explore how it all works.

item.title: How AI x ZK Will Power A New Era of Crypto with Scott Dykstra
item.description:
Blockchain systems face limitations with large complex datasets, as smart contracts weren't designed for intensive computations. Space and Time addresses this with their ZK Co-Processor, enabling smart contracts to process complex calculations while maintaining security.

This opens up practical applications: loyalty programs with historical tracking, personalized lending rates, and verifiable trading competitions. Instead of relying on intermediaries, the system provides mathematical proof of accurate calculations.

We spoke with Scott Dykstra of Space and Time about the implications for smart contracts and DeFi's evolution.

Let's explore what this means for blockchain technology.

item.itunes:summary:
Blockchain systems face limitations with large complex datasets, as smart contracts weren't designed for intensive computations. Space and Time addresses this with their ZK Co-Processor, enabling smart contracts to process complex calculations while maintaining security.

This opens up practical applications: loyalty programs with historical tracking, personalized lending rates, and verifiable trading competitions. Instead of relying on intermediaries, the system provides mathematical proof of accurate calculations.

We spoke with Scott Dykstra of Space and Time about the implications for smart contracts and DeFi's evolution.

Let's explore what this means for blockchain technology.

item.title: Why ZK Proof Adoption Will Explode in 2025
item.description:
Zero-knowledge proofs are evolving from complex cryptographic tools into practical blockchain solutions. Like the evolution from mainframe computers to smartphones, ZK proofs are transforming how we approach crypto technology.

RiskZero and Irreducible are leading this change through innovations in binary fields and hardware acceleration, making ZK proofs as accessible as email. Their advancements could enable:

-Real-time proof generation on phones

-Automatic DeFi transaction verification

-Simplified cross-chain communication

-Universal computation verification across chains

This shift could replace traditional blockchain consensus with efficient proving markets, revolutionizing how we handle trustless verification in crypto.

Join us as we explore these developments and their impact on computational economics with the teams driving this transformation.

item.title: The Geopolitical Bitcoin Space Race with Muneeb Ali
item.description:
Today's episode takes a deep dive into the next era of Bitcoin, the network, and BTC the asset.

As Bitcoin transitions from retail speculation to institutional adoption, new infrastructure is quietly reshaping its capabilities. Stacks stands at the forefront of this evolution.

BitVM and its iterations are progressing faster than expected, turning theoretical discussions into practical solutions. While initial L2 hype has cooled, the underlying technology continues to advance, creating opportunities that many have overlooked.

We feel that the next 18 months will be very important for top Bitcoin scaling teams to prove their worth and expand their marketshare, with a rising BTC. This will likely coincide with a massive bid from nation-states as they start to "FOMO" to create strategic Bitcoin reserves globally.

What a time to be alive.

Today we're diving deep with Muneeb from Stacks to explore Bitcoin's institutional evolution and the infrastructure enabling it.

Enjoy.

item.itunes:summary:
Today's episode takes a deep dive into the next era of Bitcoin, the network, and BTC the asset.

As Bitcoin transitions from retail speculation to institutional adoption, new infrastructure is quietly reshaping its capabilities. Stacks stands at the forefront of this evolution.

BitVM and its iterations are progressing faster than expected, turning theoretical discussions into practical solutions. While initial L2 hype has cooled, the underlying technology continues to advance, creating opportunities that many have overlooked.

We feel that the next 18 months will be very important for top Bitcoin scaling teams to prove their worth and expand their marketshare, with a rising BTC. This will likely coincide with a massive bid from nation-states as they start to "FOMO" to create strategic Bitcoin reserves globally.

What a time to be alive.

Today we're diving deep with Muneeb from Stacks to explore Bitcoin's institutional evolution and the infrastructure enabling it.

Enjoy.

item.title: America’s Crypto Golden Era with Stani Kulechov and Omer Goldberg
item.description:
For today's episode, we discuss the rise of Aave and a new era of crypto in America.

Trump is President! Aave turns 5! We caught up with Aave founder Stani Kulechov and Chaos Labs' Omer Goldberg to talk about the Trump Effect on DeFi, what's new in Aave V4, and where DeFAI is headed.

World Liberty Finance, the Trump Family DeFi business set to launch later this year, will provide a white-labeled, Aave powered lending market to the newest cohort of Americans onchain. We cover the World Liberty Finance deal in detail and cover Aave’s “friendly forks” program for other projects to build their own lending markets using Aave's tech. These forks share revenue with the Aave DAO.

What else is new on Aave? V4's hub-and-spoke system. Think of it as a central pool of assets that powers multichain lending markets. Plus, they're rolling out smarter interest rates that adjust based on how risky the collateral is. This could mean lower rates, and higher LTV caps across the board.

Behind the scenes, Chaos Labs is crucial to Aave's risk management with advanced simulations and auto-adjusting parameters for the T1 lending market. This is vital as Aave grows across 20+ networks and prepares for potential regulatory shifts under a Trump administration, which could mean more institutional adoption and therefore high demand for global risk management.

Whether you're building on Aave, using it regularly, or just curious about crypto under the Trump admin, let's dive into what makes this lending protocol tick and the role it could play in finance over the next four years.

item.title: Superchain 2025 Economic Outlook with Mark Tyneway
item.description:
Today, we're diving deep into Optimism's Superchain with Mark Tyneway, who's been leading efforts to revolutionize how blockchain networks interact. Mark shares insights from his work with the Ethereum Interop Forum and breaks down why we might be overcomplicating decentralization.

The Superchain vision? Making different blockchain networks work together as seamlessly as apps on your phone. No more complex bridges or complicated asset transfers. Mark explains how Optimism is turning this vision into reality, while also touching on upcoming Ethereum improvements like Pectra and PureDIS that will boost network capacity.

We also explore how the OP token plays a crucial role in governing the Superchain ecosystem and funding impactful projects.

Whether you're a developer or just curious about the future of blockchain infrastructure, Mark offers valuable insights into how Superchain is reshaping the landscape.

Let's dive in.

Today, we're diving deep into Optimism's Superchain with Mark Tyneway, who's been leading efforts to revolutionize how blockchain networks interact. Mark shares insights from his work with the Ethereum Interop Forum and breaks down why we might be overcomplicating decentralization.

The Superchain vision? Making different blockchain networks work together as seamlessly as apps on your phone. No more complex bridges or complicated asset transfers. Mark explains how Optimism is turning this vision into reality, while also touching on upcoming Ethereum improvements like Pectra and PureDIS that will boost network capacity.

We also explore how the OP token plays a crucial role in governing the Superchain ecosystem and funding impactful projects.

Whether you're a developer or just curious about the future of blockchain infrastructure, Mark offers valuable insights into how Superchain is reshaping the landscape.

Let's dive in.

item.title: Tarun Chitra vs. DeSci Debate with Benji Leibowitz
item.description:
For today's episode, we explore whether or not the saying: "Most DeSci projects today are just ICOs in a lab coat" is truth or an overexaggeration.

When Tarun Chitra dropped this line during our chat, the Pump.Science founder Benji Lebowitz nearly hopped out of his seat. What followed was one of the most fascinating debates we've had on the show about where crypto tools meet scientific research.

If you've been following the rise of decentralized science (DeSci), you know it's generating serious buzz - and serious skepticism. Can blockchain really fix science funding? Are tokenized research papers the future or just another crypto flex?

Today's episode cuts through the hype. Tarun brings his signature brutal honesty about why most DeSci projects are missing the mark on accountability. Meanwhile, Benji shows us live demos of how his team at Pump.Science is literally streaming experiments to prove their research isn't vaporware.

The parallels to early DeFi experiments are fascinating - and potentially warning signs we should heed.

Whether you're a scientist tired of grant politics, a builder curious about new token models, or just someone who wants to understand if DeSci could be the next big thing - this episode is your crash course in what's really happening at the intersection of science and crypto.

item.title: Programmable IP In The Age of AI with Jason Zhao
item.description:
For today's episode, we were joined by Jason Zhao of Story Protocol to discuss the intersection of IP and AI.

The convergence of blockchain, AI, and creative content isn't just reshaping how we think about intellectual property—it's creating the next major frontier in crypto. While others chase the latest DeFi trends, Story has emerged as one of the most strategically positioned projects of this cycle, led by a16z for the third consecutive fundraising round —a distinction shared only with Coinbase in the firm's crypto portfolio.

What makes Story particularly compelling is its unique position as the only serious AI chain bet of this cycle. In a landscape where everyone is trying to capture value from the AI revolution, Story stands out by solving a fundamental problem: how to make intellectual property tradable and yield-bearing in a global market. This isn't just another L1—it's the essential infrastructure that could unlock the floodgates for meaningful AI adoption in blockchain.

Think about the scale here:

Story isn't just building another smart contract platform—it's creating an entirely new market for IP as a yield-bearing asset, with potential value flows that could dwarf traditional L1 metrics.

What makes this particularly powerful is how Story transforms IP from a static asset into programmable, yield-generating collateral. While the world grapples with questions about AI training data and content rights, Story Protocol is quietly building the infrastructure that could make legitimate AI training and content monetization not just possible, but seamless and profitable.

In this deep dive, we'll explore how Story could fundamentally reshape the intersection of AI and blockchain, creating new possibilities for creators, developers, and investors alike. What we're witnessing isn't just another protocol launch—it's potentially the birth of a new primitive in the digital economy.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
For today's episode, we were joined by Jason Zhao of Story Protocol to discuss the intersection of IP and AI.

The convergence of blockchain, AI, and creative content isn't just reshaping how we think about intellectual property—it's creating the next major frontier in crypto. While others chase the latest DeFi trends, Story has emerged as one of the most strategically positioned projects of this cycle, led by a16z for the third consecutive fundraising round —a distinction shared only with Coinbase in the firm's crypto portfolio.

What makes Story particularly compelling is its unique position as the only serious AI chain bet of this cycle. In a landscape where everyone is trying to capture value from the AI revolution, Story stands out by solving a fundamental problem: how to make intellectual property tradable and yield-bearing in a global market. This isn't just another L1—it's the essential infrastructure that could unlock the floodgates for meaningful AI adoption in blockchain.

Think about the scale here:

Story isn't just building another smart contract platform—it's creating an entirely new market for IP as a yield-bearing asset, with potential value flows that could dwarf traditional L1 metrics.

What makes this particularly powerful is how Story transforms IP from a static asset into programmable, yield-generating collateral. While the world grapples with questions about AI training data and content rights, Story Protocol is quietly building the infrastructure that could make legitimate AI training and content monetization not just possible, but seamless and profitable.

In this deep dive, we'll explore how Story could fundamentally reshape the intersection of AI and blockchain, creating new possibilities for creators, developers, and investors alike. What we're witnessing isn't just another protocol launch—it's potentially the birth of a new primitive in the digital economy.

item.title: 2025 Crypto & AI Predictions with Haseeb Qureshi
item.description:
For today's special episode, we were joined by Haseeb of Dragonfly to discuss his 2025 predictions in-depth.

The intersection of artificial intelligence and DeFi is no longer a distant future—it's happening now. As AI tools become more sophisticated, they're fundamentally changing how developers approach smart contracts, how projects structure token launches, and how we think about the future of blockchain execution environments.

While AI-powered development tools are making smart contract creation more accessible than ever—potentially cementing EVM's market dominance—emerging alternatives like Move and SVM are gaining traction.

This raises compelling questions: Will AI-assisted development favor established platforms, or will it level the playing field for newer protocols?

We also discussed how token distribution models are evolving in parallel with these technological shifts. We're witnessing a transition from simple points-based airdrops to sophisticated, KPI-driven incentives that leverage onchain data for more transparent and equitable distribution. This evolution reflects a broader trend toward data-driven tokenomics and more nuanced approaches to further onchain price discovery.

But these advancements come with their own set of challenges. As AI tools become more integral to DeFi development, we're seeing signs of a growing technological divide between early adopters and those slower to adapt.

There's also the question of AI fatigue—a phenomenon familiar from previous tech cycles. How will these dynamics influence the DeFi ecosystem's development?

In this piece, we'll explore these intersecting trends and their implications for builders, users, and the broader DeFi landscape. From the changing nature of smart contract development to the future of token distribution, we'll examine how AI is reshaping the foundations of decentralized finance—and what it means for what comes next.

item.title: How To Build A Web3 Gaming Empire With Jeff "Jihoz" Zirlin
item.description:
For today's episode, we are live from Bangkok again discussing what it takes to build a massive userbase onchain from the ground up.

Picture this: It's early days, and Axie Infinity is trying to scale on Ethereum. They experiment with Loom Network, but like many early solutions, it just can't handle their explosive growth.

Rather than compromise, they take the bold step of building their own solution - Ronin. Today, that decision has paid off spectacularly. Beyond powering Axie, Ronin now supports rising stars like Pixels, boasting 1.5 million daily active users and generating millions in monthly revenue.

What makes Ronin special isn't just its tech - it's the holistic ecosystem they've built. Every piece, from their wallet to their NFT marketplace to their DEX, was crafted with real user needs in mind. There's no unnecessary complexity, no features built just for hype. Everything serves a purpose, tested and refined in the crucible of actual usage.

The impact has been transformative, particularly in regions often overlooked by traditional tech. In the Philippines, Vietnam, and Brazil, Ronin has become more than just a gaming platform - it's an economic engine. By breathing new life into dormant NFTs and creating genuine utility through gameplay, they've built something that delivers real value to everyday users.

Picture this: It's early days, and Axie Infinity is trying to scale on Ethereum. They experiment with Loom Network, but like many early solutions, it just can't handle their explosive growth.

Rather than compromise, they take the bold step of building their own solution - Ronin. Today, that decision has paid off spectacularly. Beyond powering Axie, Ronin now supports rising stars like Pixels, boasting 1.5 million daily active users and generating millions in monthly revenue.

What makes Ronin special isn't just its tech - it's the holistic ecosystem they've built. Every piece, from their wallet to their NFT marketplace to their DEX, was crafted with real user needs in mind. There's no unnecessary complexity, no features built just for hype. Everything serves a purpose, tested and refined in the crucible of actual usage.

The impact has been transformative, particularly in regions often overlooked by traditional tech. In the Philippines, Vietnam, and Brazil, Ronin has become more than just a gaming platform - it's an economic engine. By breathing new life into dormant NFTs and creating genuine utility through gameplay, they've built something that delivers real value to everyday users.

For developers, Ronin offers more than just infrastructure - it provides a blueprint for success. Their strategy of nurturing a core "golden cohort" of users and expanding organically has proven remarkably effective.

For players, it means gaming experiences that feel natural and seamless, where the blockchain elements enhance rather than intrude.

While Ronin has had its ups and downs, its clear that they are steadfast on bringing new users onchain, which were excited about.

item.title: The Massive 'Infra to Apps' Shift in Crypto Investing with Wei Dai
item.description:
For today's podcast, we were joined by Wei Dai, a researcher at 1kx and PhD cryptographer, to discuss investing in crypto's killer apps, the shift from infra to apps, and interop.

Think of rollup clusters as the high-speed railways of blockchain - they're not merely accelerating transactions, they're fundamentally transforming how we approach value transfer across networks.

Just as railways reshaped urban development, rollup clusters are establishing more efficient and interconnected DeFi ecosystems. We'll examine three key innovations that define rollup clusters:

First, their approach to resolving the scalability trilemma.

Second, the economic architecture that ensures system sustainability.

And third, the expanding landscape of opportunities for builders and users.

Whether you're developing protocols or exploring DeFi opportunities, these developments have significant implications. We're observing these systems actively reconstruct how liquidity flows and how value is generated throughout the DeFi ecosystem.

Crypto is going through a shift from infra to apps, welcome to the app era.

item.title: Rollup-Boost, Unichain, And TEEs With Hasu & Robert Miller
item.description:
In today's episode, we explore how sometimes the best innovations come from rethinking the basics rather than fixing what already exists.


That's exactly what Flashbots is achieving with their groundbreaking innovations in the rollup space - creating something entirely new instead of patching the old.


At its core, this is about building a better trading system from the ground up. Flashbots stepped back from the usual approach of fixing individual problems and asked a fundamental question: "How can we design a blockchain specifically for trading?" Their answer is Unichain, which focuses on two essential components - optimizing transaction speed and ensuring precise trade ordering.


One of the biggest challenges in blockchain trading has been MEV, where traders can lose value due to transaction ordering issues. Flashbots has developed an innovative solution using Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) - secure computational environments that ensure fair and transparent trade processing.


The benefits of this new approach are far-reaching. Regular traders experience faster and more reliable transactions. Developers gain access to enhanced tools for building sophisticated trading applications. And the entire system operates with significantly improved efficiency.


This development signals an important shift in blockchain technology's evolution. Rather than attempting to create all-purpose blockchains, we're witnessing the emergence of specialized chains designed for specific use cases. In this instance, Unichain excels at one crucial function: enabling superior trading experiences.

item.itunes:summary:
In today's episode, we explore how sometimes the best innovations come from rethinking the basics rather than fixing what already exists.


That's exactly what Flashbots is achieving with their groundbreaking innovations in the rollup space - creating something entirely new instead of patching the old.


At its core, this is about building a better trading system from the ground up. Flashbots stepped back from the usual approach of fixing individual problems and asked a fundamental question: "How can we design a blockchain specifically for trading?" Their answer is Unichain, which focuses on two essential components - optimizing transaction speed and ensuring precise trade ordering.


One of the biggest challenges in blockchain trading has been MEV, where traders can lose value due to transaction ordering issues. Flashbots has developed an innovative solution using Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) - secure computational environments that ensure fair and transparent trade processing.


The benefits of this new approach are far-reaching. Regular traders experience faster and more reliable transactions. Developers gain access to enhanced tools for building sophisticated trading applications. And the entire system operates with significantly improved efficiency.


This development signals an important shift in blockchain technology's evolution. Rather than attempting to create all-purpose blockchains, we're witnessing the emergence of specialized chains designed for specific use cases. In this instance, Unichain excels at one crucial function: enabling superior trading experiences.


We'll explore these technological improvements in detail and examine how they're shaping the future of onchain scaling for Ethereum, in the dark forest.

item.title: Mert Mumtaz on Pudgy Penguins, Solana's Vision, and The Blockchain Endgame
item.description:
For today's episode, we sit down with Mert Mumtaz to examine Solana's technical architecture and its impact on blockchain scalability. Solana established itself by achieving high speeds and low transaction costs, challenging traditional blockchain limitations.

The platform's approach to scaling focuses on increasing bandwidth while reducing latency - a departure from conventional blockchain design. This strategy has led to innovations in block production, including a multi-proposer system and new solutions to MEV challenges.

We also discussed the Pudgy Penguins launch on Solana and learned why Mert is excited about the community growth on Solana and what really happened with the claim process which seemingly clogged Solana.

Key topics in our conversation include ZK compression implementation, managing high transaction throughput, and the practical implications for developers and users within the ecosystem. We'll explore how these technical decisions affect both current operations and future development.

Join us for a technical deep dive into Solana's blockchain architecture and its broader implications for the field.

item.title: What Is The Big FHE Unlock? With Guy Zyskind
item.description:
Privacy-enabled blockchain technology is transforming how we process sensitive data. In conversation with Guy Zyskind, we explore how Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows smart contracts to compute encrypted data while maintaining security.

Real-world applications are already emerging on Arbitrum's infrastructure - from sealed-bid auctions preventing front-running to confidential token transfers and secure payroll systems that protect sensitive information.

At the core of this development is Fhenix, whose co-processor model integrates privacy features into the Arbitrum ecosystem. This combination of scalability and privacy could fundamentally change how we build and interact with blockchain applications.

Let's examine how these technologies are shaping the future of Web3 development.

item.itunes:summary:
Privacy-enabled blockchain technology is transforming how we process sensitive data. In conversation with Guy Zyskind, we explore how Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows smart contracts to compute encrypted data while maintaining security.

Real-world applications are already emerging on Arbitrum's infrastructure - from sealed-bid auctions preventing front-running to confidential token transfers and secure payroll systems that protect sensitive information.

At the core of this development is Fhenix, whose co-processor model integrates privacy features into the Arbitrum ecosystem. This combination of scalability and privacy could fundamentally change how we build and interact with blockchain applications.

Let's examine how these technologies are shaping the future of Web3 development.

item.title: Superchain vs. Arbitrum Orbit Debate with Ryan Wyatt, A.J. Warner, and Jill Gunter
item.description:
For today's episode, we decided to up the spice levels and have some fun.


While technical specifications and token metrics often dominate L2 discussions, a more compelling story lies beneath the surface: the fundamental philosophical and strategic differences between Ethereum's leading scaling solutions, Arbitrum and Optimism.


In a recent roundtable discussion, we explored these contrasting visions with an exceptional panel:


AJ Warner from Offchain Labs

Ryan Wyatt from the Optimism Foundation

Jill from Espresso Systems


Our conversation ventured beyond typical technical analyses, delving into how these ecosystems approach critical challenges differently. From licensing strategies to cross-chain interoperability, each project reveals distinct perspectives on blockchain's future.


What emerged was a fascinating exploration of how philosophical differences shape every aspect of these platforms – from their governance structures to their approaches to ecosystem growth and innovation.


Join us as we unpack these insights and examine how two leading L2 solutions are charting different paths toward Ethereum's scaled future.

item.title: Crypto's New Valuation Frameworks with Jordi Alexander and Sam Kazemian
item.description:
For today's episode, we are discussing the evolving frameworks for understanding value in the crypto markets, with the goal of answering the following:


How do we value digital assets in an ecosystem that's constantly evolving?


We were joined with industry veterans Jordi Alexander and Sam Kazemian who both revealed fascinating insights in how we should think about crypto valuations.


Sam introduces a framework that challenges traditional categories, especially on ETH, the asset. By separating assets into "sovereign commodities" and "labor-representing tokens," he makes the claim that there are really only two types of tokens. Ethereum's position was highly debated here, as Sam thinks the Ethereum community has to rethink the way it is building the narrative for ETH the asset.


Jordi brought up the ideas of "community money" with different types of assets, and how Solana and Dogecoin have certain properties specifically. These aren't just speculative assets, but complex ecosystems driven by unique social dynamics. Jordi's insights on community engagement and credible neutrality add crucial depth to this perspective.


We also touched on VCs, unlocks, inflation, and how provenance really impacts the staying power of crypto assets.


Join us for an insightful conversation into these new crypto asset frameworks and discover how they might reshape our understanding of value in the digital age.


P.S. We've launched The Rollup Edge for our dedicated listeners: early episode access, podcast transcripts, ad-free listening on a custom RSS feed, and a members lounge all for $14/month.

item.dc:creator: Where digital assets and finance converge. Hosted by Andy and Robbie.
item.itunes:summary:
For today's episode, we are discussing the evolving frameworks for understanding value in the crypto markets, with the goal of answering the following:


How do we value digital assets in an ecosystem that's constantly evolving?


We were joined with industry veterans Jordi Alexander and Sam Kazemian who both revealed fascinating insights in how we should think about crypto valuations.


Sam introduces a framework that challenges traditional categories, especially on ETH, the asset. By separating assets into "sovereign commodities" and "labor-representing tokens," he makes the claim that there are really only two types of tokens. Ethereum's position was highly debated here, as Sam thinks the Ethereum community has to rethink the way it is building the narrative for ETH the asset.


Jordi brought up the ideas of "community money" with different types of assets, and how Solana and Dogecoin have certain properties specifically. These aren't just speculative assets, but complex ecosystems driven by unique social dynamics. Jordi's insights on community engagement and credible neutrality add crucial depth to this perspective.


We also touched on VCs, unlocks, inflation, and how provenance really impacts the staying power of crypto assets.


Join us for an insightful conversation into these new crypto asset frameworks and discover how they might reshape our understanding of value in the digital age.


P.S. We've launched The Rollup Edge for our dedicated listeners: early episode access, podcast transcripts, ad-free listening on a custom RSS feed, and a members lounge all for $14/month.

item.title: Steven Goldfeder on Arbitrum’s Lore, Orbit Appchain Thesis, and DeFi Renaissance
item.description: In today’s video, we are joined by Steven Goldfeder to discuss scaling Ethereum. Steven Goldfeder joins us to examine Ethereum scaling through Arbitrum's journey - from Princeton research paper to production infrastructure. We'll analyze Orbit's technical architecture, which enables customizable chain deployments, and evaluate their "community source" licensing approach. The discussion explores both opportunities and challenges in their vision of interconnected chain networks. This conversation cuts through the hype to examine how academic research translates into real-world blockchain infrastructure. item.title: Why Based Rollups Are Ethereum's Best Bet with Sam Battenally
item.description: For today's episode, were taking a deep dive into based rollups to answer the following question: Could the next breakthrough in Ethereum scaling come from working with the network rather than around it? While most rollup solutions build separate consensus layers, an intriguing new approach called based rollups takes a different path – leveraging Ethereum's existing validator network to sequence blocks. Rather than creating parallel consensus mechanisms, based rollups tap directly into Ethereum's established validator set. This creates a more cohesive ecosystem where rollups share both infrastructure and security. The Rise team is pioneering this approach with innovations like parallel EVM engines and versioned Merkle trees. Their solution becomes particularly compelling as more based rollups join the ecosystem, and better composability properties are unlocked. The benefits compound naturally – each new participant contributes to shared security costs and improves liquidity efficiency. This network effect, combined with the emergence of the "GigaGas era," could enable entirely new categories of blockchain applications. Enjoy. item.itunes:summary: For today's episode, were taking a deep dive into based rollups to answer the following question: Could the next breakthrough in Ethereum scaling come from working with the network rather than around it? While most rollup solutions build separate consensus layers, an intriguing new approach called based rollups takes a different path – leveraging Ethereum's existing validator network to sequence blocks. Rather than creating parallel consensus mechanisms, based rollups tap directly into Ethereum's established validator set. This creates a more cohesive ecosystem where rollups share both infrastructure and security. The Rise team is pioneering this approach with innovations like parallel EVM engines and versioned Merkle trees. Their solution becomes particularly compelling as more based rollups join the ecosystem, and better composability properties are unlocked. The benefits compound naturally – each new participant contributes to shared security costs and improves liquidity efficiency. This network effect, combined with the emergence of the "GigaGas era," could enable entirely new categories of blockchain applications. Enjoy. item.title: How To Become The Best Crypto Investor Of All Time with Santiago Santos
item.description:
Beyond protocols and price charts, today's episode dives into navigating crypto as an investor, builder, and human being.


Our conversation with Santi spans from deeply personal insights on mental health and finding meaning, to why crypto remains one of today's most transformative industries. At its core is a powerful message about belief - the conviction that you can excel in your chosen path, especially in a space where merit trumps credentials.


But thriving in crypto isn't just about technical skills or market timing. It's a psychological game that demands emotional resilience, the ability to learn from mistakes, and lifestyle choices that support long-term success.


We explore how memes drive adoption, the crypto-AI convergence, and why cases like Ripple's success signal a potential retail return. For Santi, crypto transcends investment - it's a socioeconomic revolution that demands both practical wisdom and a vision for transforming business and society.


This episode connects personal growth with practical investing, while never losing sight of crypto's bigger promise.


Join us as we unpack lessons from someone who's been in the trenches of this revolutionary space.

item.title: How Fast Confirmations Will Improve Rollup UX with Ben Fisch and Matt Pearring
item.description:
Today's episode explores how the rollup-centric vision for Ethereum brought massive scalability gains, but also new challenges - from fragmented liquidity to complex coordination across execution layers.


Enter Espresso and Arbitrum's collaboration, tackling these hurdles head-on. At its core is Espresso's fast confirmation system, enabling rollups to validate transactions with both speed and strong security. This unlocks true interoperability without sacrificing decentralization.


Their work extends to democratizing sequencers, a critical step toward Ethereum's ideals of neutrality and censorship resistance. By making sequencers accountable while maintaining performance, they're showing how rollups can evolve thoughtfully.


The introduction of standards like ERC-7683 for intent-based interoperability demonstrates how small, strategic improvements can have outsized impact. As Arbitrum pushes toward deeper decentralization, their partnership with Espresso exemplifies how modular innovation can advance Ethereum's vision while keeping things practical.


This isn't just about technical upgrades - it's about shaping how rollups will actually work for users and developers in the real world.


A composable future is coming for Ethereum.

item.itunes:summary:
Today's episode explores how the rollup-centric vision for Ethereum brought massive scalability gains, but also new challenges - from fragmented liquidity to complex coordination across execution layers.


Enter Espresso and Arbitrum's collaboration, tackling these hurdles head-on. At its core is Espresso's fast confirmation system, enabling rollups to validate transactions with both speed and strong security. This unlocks true interoperability without sacrificing decentralization.


Their work extends to democratizing sequencers, a critical step toward Ethereum's ideals of neutrality and censorship resistance. By making sequencers accountable while maintaining performance, they're showing how rollups can evolve thoughtfully.


The introduction of standards like ERC-7683 for intent-based interoperability demonstrates how small, strategic improvements can have outsized impact. As Arbitrum pushes toward deeper decentralization, their partnership with Espresso exemplifies how modular innovation can advance Ethereum's vision while keeping things practical.


This isn't just about technical upgrades - it's about shaping how rollups will actually work for users and developers in the real world.


A composable future is coming for Ethereum.

item.title: AggLayer Mainnet Launch Is Coming With Marc Boiron
item.description:
The blockchain landscape is evolving beyond isolated chains and fragmented liquidity. Enter AggLayer - a framework reimagining how rollups and chains interact.


But why does this matter?


AggLayer isn't just another interoperability solution. It's a foundational layer that lets chains share network effects while maintaining their independence. Think of it as the invisible infrastructure that makes cross-chain activity feel native and seamless.


At its core lies pessimistic proofing - a breakthrough that enables secure cross-chain transactions without heavy computational overhead. This means established networks like Polygon POS can integrate seamlessly, bringing their massive user base and liquidity into the broader ecosystem.


The innovation doesn't stop there. With ZK proofs powering sub-5-second cross-chain transactions, AggLayer is setting new standards for speed and trust. Users might never interact with it directly, but they'll feel its impact through faster, cheaper experiences across chains.


Polygon's role here is crucial. Their suite of solutions - from POS to ZK EVM - brings vital liquidity and tooling to AggLayer's foundation. Combined with open-source advances like Plonky3 driving ZK adoption, we're seeing the blueprint for truly unified blockchain ecosystems.


Curious about the future of chain interoperability? Want to understand how projects like Polygon are architecting app-centric experiences?


Join us as we explore AggLayer's pivotal role in shaping what's next.

item.title: Nick White and Jon Charbonneau on The Rise of Celestia's Native Ecosystem
item.description:
In today's episode, we explore the next evolution of the modular blockchain landscape with Nick White and Jon Charbonneu. Celestia's base layer now supports 21 chains and is pushing sovereign rollups as the next step. As a minimalist data availability focused L1, Celestia has had a big year with a lot yet to come.


Our conversation explores the mechanics behind Celestia's blockchain design, from lazybridging to ZK accounts. We talk about the next evolution of the Celestia roadmap, focused on building a native ecosystem of interoperable rollups. The rise of altVMs, Celestia's recent upgrades, and light nodes were also touched on.


Towards the end, we discuss TIA, the asset, and how it is used in the Celestia ecosystem as well as how Jon thinks about valuing it amongst other base layer assets.

item.itunes:summary:
In today's episode, we explore the next evolution of the modular blockchain landscape with Nick White and Jon Charbonneu. Celestia's base layer now supports 21 chains and is pushing sovereign rollups as the next step. As a minimalist data availability focused L1, Celestia has had a big year with a lot yet to come.


Our conversation explores the mechanics behind Celestia's blockchain design, from lazybridging to ZK accounts. We talk about the next evolution of the Celestia roadmap, focused on building a native ecosystem of interoperable rollups. The rise of altVMs, Celestia's recent upgrades, and light nodes were also touched on.


Towards the end, we discuss TIA, the asset, and how it is used in the Celestia ecosystem as well as how Jon thinks about valuing it amongst other base layer assets.
